items.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered: Still the Open-World Game to Beat?
items.summary: As great as CD Projekt RED's remastered classic is, how does it stack up to the best open-world titles from the past decade?
items.content:
I n case you haven’t heard, I’m rather…obsessed with The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , especially after the free Remastered update. Even with its issues, it brings a more contemporary look, and its many new gameplay additions bring it in line with some of the best the genre has to offer. Of course, that only raises the question: How exactly does it compare to the very best open-world games of yesteryear?

We’ve already seen how Geralt’s journey matches up against Crimson Desert , especially with the latter receiving its own massive Enhanced update. But what about CD Projekt RED’s own Cyberpunk 2077 ? Red Dead Redemption 2 ? The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom ? Ghost of Tsushima ? Elden Ring ? Or better yet, all of them? Let’s find out, starting with…

Elden Ring’s world-building, especially the environmental storytelling and lore, deserves a nod, and we admit that Tears of the Kingdom is a better tale than Breath of the Wild . But in terms of emotional investment in the plot, how the stories connect to the world, and the meaningful decisions you can make, the biggest competition in this category is obviously Cyberpunk 2077, Red Dead Redemption 2, and Ghost of Tsushima .

As much as I liked Jin Sakai and his conflict between honor and saving his people, he has little choice (except in the ending). Red Dead Redemption 2 and Cyberpunk 2077 both offer incredible characters, and it’s honestly neck and neck with the best The Witcher 3 has to offer. Night City has a slight edge because of the more extensive choices and consequences. But in terms of storytelling, it’s probably on par with Red Dead Redemption 2 in scale, emotional investment, pacing, dialogue, etc.

If there’s anything all of these games do very well, it’s exploration and discovery. Following the Guiding Wind on Tsushima to turn up an enemy camp, hot spring or mystery; discovering random events in Red Dead Redemption 2 or just plain creepy occurrences alongside the many side missions; and getting to know the messy ins and outs of Night City have proven extremely enjoyable over the years.

That said, Elden Ring and Tears of the Kingdom are probably the standard-bearers. The former’s boss fights, weapons, spells, and that sense of continuously pushing forward, just to see what’s next. The latter with its discoveries, puzzles, sights, and much more across three different planes of existence. I wouldn’t say The Witcher 3 Remastered is on the same level in terms of puzzles or even boss fights, but it’s stories, especially in terms of writing, are certainly a notch above either. Even the most innocuous of contracts and treasure hunts can lead to unexpected twists and turns.

Regardless, in exploration, I’d put it on par again with Red Dead Redemption 2 and above Cyberpunk 2077 and Ghost of Tsushima , as the kings of the genre continue to rule.

Right off the bat, Ghost of Tsushima falters. As detailed as the NPCs look and as gorgeous as the world can be, there’s very little interaction with the environment. Similarly, NPCs don’t really respond to your reactions outside of quests, so you can’t suddenly slay the residents of Tsushima. It’s a beautiful backdrop for a great story, but that’s it.

Comparatively, Red Dead Redemption 2 lets you run wild and kill regular NPCs, but with little consequence, as the main characters go scot-free (unless the plot dictates otherwise). On the other hand, from your looks to the last time Arthur showered, the world is responsive and treats you accordingly. The same goes depending on whether you’re honorable or not. That’s in sharp contrast to Elden Ring , where you can murder most NPCs, even those with extensive side quests, though the main quest keeps going. Of course, the world of RDR2 excels because of the sheer attention to detail, thanks to Rockstar’s insane dedication and budget.

On the other hand, Tears of the Kingdom boasts a believable world in terms of weather, physics, and so on. Create a large fire and its updraft allows for gliding. Carry any metal in a thunderstorm, and you’ll be struck by lightning. Those are only the basics, though – we’re not even talking about things like constructing massive Zonaite machines to rain death or exploiting shield hopping to solve puzzles. But aside from yeeting Koroks, you can’t really affect NPCs.

Even next to Cyberpunk 2077, The Witcher 3’s environmental interaction and responses from the world are a step lower. NPCs can still act realistically, but you can forget about killing them. The only effect you’ll have on the world is probably setting fires with Igni or breaking walls with Aard. At least it’s visually believable enough, whether it’s water realistically dripping down clothes, how foliage interacts with wind and other weather phenomena, and more.

With how wildly different each game’s combat can be, it’s hard to really earmark a clear winner. After all, I liked Cyberpunk 2077’s shooting, but even with solid melee combat, The Witcher 3 is handled completely differently. Elden Ring’s combat remains stellar, but that’s a Souls-like with a completely different rule-set. Red Dead Redemption 2 is a third-person shooter where cover is important; Tears of the Kingdom is more action-adventure hack-and-slash – it’s tough. Perhaps the closest comparison is Ghost of Tsushima , even with the latter’s stance-based combat.

However, even with the Remastered’s various improvements, there’s no denying that The Witcher 3’s combat isn’t its strongest quality. More responsive and smoother, sure, but better than Tsushima, Elden Ring or Cyberpunk ? No. At the very least, based on mechanical preference, I’d place it slightly above Tears and RDR2 .

Player freedom can be a lot more important than one realizes in open-world titles nowadays. Red Dead Redemption 2 offers a range of activities to get lost in, and depending on how you get involved, some circumstances may change. However, the main story proceeds exactly how it should, and any attempt to deviate usually results in failure.

Circana has released a listing of the top ten best-selling games in the U.S. for the month of August 2026.

Sports games have always been popular in the states, so it’s no surprise that NBA 2K27 and Madden NFL 27 lead the way. They take up the top two spots.

Elden Ring was previously at 41 last month. But boosted by the Nintendo Switch 2 launch, the game is now at #7. We also see Mario Kart World and Splatoon Raiders on the list.

Here’s a look at the complete list of best-selling games in the U.S. for August 2026:

1. NBA 2K27 – Take-Two Interactive 2. Madden NFL 27 – EA 3. Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls – Sony 4. Kickoff Bundle (2026) – EA 5. Star Wars: Zero Company – EA 6. Halo: Campaign Evolved – Microsoft 7. Also, for those wondering, here’s a look at the overall best sellers of 2026 so far:

items.title: Spending On Physical Games In The U.S. Is…Up? Thanks To Game-Key Cards?
items.content:
Big Walk Elden Ring Madden Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls NBA 2k27

In a weird twist, apparently consumer spending on new physical video games in the U.S. is actually up 5 percent year-over-year so far in 2026, and it’s mostly thanks to game-key cards.

Okay, it’s mostly thanks to there being way more game-key cards available than before, and the Switch 2…existing.

This comes from Circana, which reports the 5-percent increase on new physical software as largely due to a whopping 631-percent increase in spending on game-key cards, offsetting a 3-percent drop in everything else.

But that number sounded very suspicious, so I asked Circana’s Mat Piscatella what was up.

“Last year there were 10 titles published as Game-Key Cards,” he replied. “This year 54 more Game-Key Card titles have been published. So that’s the biggest reason. So, we are seeing new physical software sales showing growth for the first time in more than a decade. But that’s being driven primarily by Switch 2 and publishers leaning more into Game-Key Cards.”

So, yeah, Switch 2 is out, people want to buy more physical games on it than they do other consoles, there are more games available now than there were last year, and a lot of them are game-key cards. That explains that. (But if Sony asks, it’s totally because physical media is back in.)

Overall spending on content for just the month of August was down 10 percent, mostly due to a big drop in mobile spending, but console content spending was also down. PC was up, as was subscription spending. NBA 2K27 was the best-selling game of August, followed by Madden NFL 27, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, Madden’s Kickoff Bundle, and Star Wars Zero Company, in that order. Big month for new launches! NBA 2K27 is also now the third best-selling game of the year thus far.

Elden Ring jumped from 41st in July to 7th in August thanks to its Switch 2 release, and Piscatella tells me that Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 ranked 11th, up from 31st, thanks to hype from the recent film. Kingdom Hearts Integrum Masterpiece also had a huge leap, from 159th to 26th, thanks to D23’s big reveals and a Steam sale.

Oh, and look! Big Walk cracked the top 10! That’s kinda nuts for an indie like that!

Total spending was down 9 percent year-over-year to $4.3 billion due to a drop in mobile and console content spending, offset by PC content spending being up

Accessories spending was up 3 percent, and total hardware spending was down 3 percent. PS5 dollar sales were up 17 percent but Xbox and Switch 2 spending dropped 13 percent and offset that. Also, that’s spending, so taking price increases into consideration. Unit sales were pretty dismal: down 15 percent year-over-year in the lowest total for an August month since 2013. PlayStation hardware was down 11 percent (also the lowest since 2013), Xbox was down 31 percent (lowest since 2020), and Nintendo was down 15 percent. The average price for a new unit of hardware was $541. Yikes.

items.title: AI Video Game Mod Mashups Are Taking Off—Here Are the Wackiest Examples
items.summary: Minecraft in Elden Ring, Skate in Call of Duty, and Spider-Man in Gotham. AI vibe coders are creating crazy video game mashup mods.
items.content:
News Gaming AI Video Game Mod Mashups Are Taking Off—Here Are the Wackiest Examples Minecraft in Elden Ring, Skate in Call of Duty, and Spider-Man in Gotham. AI vibe coders are creating crazy video game mashup mods. By Ryan S. Gladwin Edited by Stephen Graves Oct 8, 2026 Oct 8, 2026 4 min read Call of Duty in Minecraft. Credit: @DramaAlert Create an account to save your articles. Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. In brief Video game modders are combining classic games to create fun, weird, and wacky mashups that are going viral on social media. Gamers are fighting bosses in Elden Ring with Minecraft swords, skateboarding around Call of Duty maps, and swinging around Gotham City as Spider-Man. It's made possible through the use of Claude-based AI agents that help users to vibe code mod mashups in a matter of hours. Social media has exploded with wacky video game mods that combine titles the public never thought they'd see together. People are driving Mario Kart vehicles in Call of Duty Zombies, fighting Elden Ring bosses with Minecraft characters, and even swinging around Batman's Gotham City as Spider-Man.

This is all possible thanks to gamers using Claude AI agents to vibe code the mods from the ground up. Merging games uses a "passthrough mod," according to a popular GitHub guide, which runs the two games simultaneously, with one hosting the world while the other supplies the gameplay—i.e., movement and combat.

Vibe coding requires the user to tell the AI model what they want, test the outcomes, and provide feedback—leaving the AI model to do all the coding itself. The GitHub guide claims it took three to four hours to merge Elden Ring and Spider-Man, although it warned that first results are often rough around the edges.

Some gamers say that this is "one of the coolest things I’ve seen in gaming in 10+ years" and that it marks the dawn of "the renaissance of gaming." Here are some of the best AI video game modding mashups.

One of the first mashups to go viral combined cult classic Skate with Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, allowing gamers to skateboard across their favourite maps.

"Imagine hitting a trick shot with this. We will see clips soon, any moment now," one X user posted . "This is the greatest thing that will ever happen in Call of Duty," another said .

AI HACKERS HAVE PUT SKATEBOARDING IN CALL OF DUTY MODERN WARFARE 2! 🚨

ITS TIME TO PACE THE FRONTIER. @DarioAmodei @sama @elonmusk @theo pic.twitter.com/vYTS2YnJKG

Perhaps the most viral of all the video game merges is Minecraft in Elden Ring.

With this mod, not only can you use Minecraft weapons and teleport with an Ender Pearl, but you can access 1,600 Minecraft items, create fully functioning redstone contraptions, and even enter creative mode. That's not to mention you can spawn mobs using eggs, meaning creepers can fight Elden Ring's iconic boss Malenia for you.

Bored of the Minecraft options? The mod also allows you to add in Black Ops guns, so you can quickly switch between Minecraft and Call of Duty weapons in the heat of battle.

Unfortunately, its creator, Toby Jacobs, has yet to release the mod to the public. He claims to be open to the idea, but says he'll have to create a Windows port as it was developed for Mac.

I put the entire of game minecraft into elden ring as mod. its runs on Mac. pic.twitter.com/CojefjxtLn

— Anime Girl Worshiper (@TobynJacobs) September 29, 2026

items.title: Opinion: Elden Ring Is One Of My Favourite Games That I've Hardly Played
items.content:
I have started a new Elden Ring save file on four separate occasions now, and I have absolutely adored my time with each of them. And yet, despite putting 15-20 hours minimum into each new load, my current Switch 2 playthrough is the first time that I've managed to push through the 'tutorial area'.

I need to do some explaining here, because if you have never ventured into the Lands Between, then three save files and 60+ hours spent in a tutorial sounds insane. However, in the grand scheme of things, it's not that bad .

After pushing you through a very brief 'real' tutorial — one that introduces you to the basics of Elden Ring's combat and movement — your Tarnished avatar is funnelled into Limgrave and beckoned towards Stormveil Castle as your first major objective. However, rushing straight to the battlements will put you up against foes and challenges that you are severely underprepared for, so the game encourages you to instead take a stroll around the area and perhaps venture down to the locales south of it in the Weeping Peninsula.

Much like Breath of the Wild 's Great Plateau, this is the game's actual tutorial. But I cannot stress this enough, it makes Link's wakeup spot look tiny.

Limgrave and its surrounding areas are huge and so densely packed with things to do that one could happily play this zone as a game of its own. Heck, for my first three save files, that's exactly what I did.

I explored the nooks and crannies of all the region's catacombs, took on mini bosses and Minor Erdtrees, solved environmental puzzles to unlock new gear, and took on sidequests that involved storylines and platforming challenges of their own.

On my first save back in 2022, by the time that I finally pushed through the game's first 'roadblock' boss, Margit (yes, there is a way around him, but I didn't see that at the time), I was quite content with the 20-odd hours I had put into Elden Ring, and I went off to play something else. Save files two and three saw me go further still, through the game's first real dungeon and into the boss on the other side. On both these occasions, I polished off Godrick the Grafted (a proper FromSoft name, if I've ever heard one) with relative ease, but was deterred by what awaited me afterwards: the proper game .

Just like the first time that you paraglide off the Great Plateau and realise everything you've explored up to this point is just a tiny proportion of what the whole map has to offer, stepping into Lunaria of the Lakes is a similarly daunting task. The zone's entry point even has a vantage point vaguely reminiscent of leaving the Shrine of Resurrection, for crying out loud.

For save files two and three, the scope of what was to come was simply too much. I had had a wonderful time with everything I had played up until that point, and loved how it all culminated in a challenging dungeon and gruesome boss. Honestly, I couldn't bring myself to do it all over again.

Until the Tarnished Edition arrived on Switch 2, that is. I finally got around to starting save file number four a few weeks back, and believe me when I say, I have not been able to put it down.

I did my usual Limgrave exploration, ventured into the fiery Caelid region (and swiftly realised I was still far too weak for it), and steadily levelled up in various catacombs and hoard encounters. Unsurprisingly, I dispatched both Margit and Godrick in one or two attempts — I've played 'em both more than enough by now — and Stormveil was similarly breezy for someone who's spent so much time in it over the years. But then something unexpected happened: I kept playing.

Despite my previous cowardice, I stepped boldly into the uncharted waters of 'The Lakes' and I still haven't quit. As I am writing this, I have just polished off The Academy of Raya Lucaria (a dungeon that, as someone using a magic build, can get in the bin) and its Good Boi / Bad Gurl bosses, and I still want more.

Aside from the portability perk — I couldn't put this version down, even if I wanted to — the Switch 2 port itself is absolutely sublime. All those months of convention footage and delays had me worried that I'd never be able to play a game this reliant on reaction times with a choppy frame rate, but it all holds up remarkably well. Performance certainly hasn't been perfect, and I have encountered some substantial drops here and there, but I'm finding myself enjoying this version even more than my prior attempts on PS4 and PS5 (and I loved those attempts).

Having spoken to some friends that are absolutely head-over-heels for this game, I know that I am very much still in the early stages of what Elden Ring has to offer, and there's every chance that I'll butt up against another roadblock down the line and bring save file four to an end.

items.title: Hell Is Officially Breaking Loose For The Gaming Industry Thanks To AI
items.summary: Viral games like Minecraft inside Elden Ring, PS5 emulators, and recent jailbreaks do not bode well for Sony, Microsoft, or Nintendo
items.content:
By Patricia Hernandez Published Oct 6, 2026, 2:30 PM EDT Patricia is the former editor-in-chief of Kotaku , where she spent a decade writing and editing. Prior to that, she served as the Culture Editor at Polygon , and as a reporter at The Verge . Hernandez specializes in Pokémon TCG, Nintendo, and offbeat internet culture stories. News Viral games like Minecraft inside Elden Ring, PS5 emulators, and recent jailbreaks can all be tied to Claude in some way

Graphic: Grant Walkup/Polygon | Source images: Sony Interactive Entertainment PlayStation 5 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 19 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap There's an upheaval happening in the video game industry right now, and it's a major threat to publishers and video game developers alike. The outcome of this paradigm shift won't be fully evident for years, but the cause is obvious: Artificial intelligence has advanced faster than anyone anticipated.

Perhaps you've witnessed this seismic event without even realizing it. The last week or so has seen an explosion of projects that combine mainstream video games into fully playable experiences that don't even sound real. Super Mario 64 in Elden Ring . Tony Hawk's Pro Skater in Call of Duty. Minecraft inside Pokémon. Marvel's Spider-Man inside Batman: Arkham Asylum .

All of these fever-dream amalgamations are the product of Claude Opus 5.5, which was released back on Sept. 22. Opus is powerful enough that users can reverse-engineer projects at incredible speed. What Opus does is technically possible for a human, but would normally take years. Opus instead needs only a few minutes to figure out how game developers built the gameplay mechanics and infrastructure holding together relatively modern video games.

Many of these games shouldn't be compatible with one another, as they are composed of different building blocks. After Opus figures out how a game works, it can essentially build a script bridge that translates each individual game's quirks, like the animation and physics, into a language that the other game can understand. Critically, much of this has been made possible by the release of third-party tools like the Universal Modder, which streamlines all the processes an AI needs to combine games into a single package.

As these gaming mashups proliferate, Sony has found itself at the center of an intellectual property fight. The same technology that makes those game combinations possible is also partially to blame for the sudden advances in PlayStation 5 emulators on PC. Projects like SharpEmu and KytyPS5 are both human-driven efforts built from scratch, and these tools allow PCs to boot and run PS5 games at native 4K resolution.

These emulators have limitations, and some of the earliest playable game projects can be glitchy. The innovations nonetheless undergird more pinpointed efforts to make games like Infamous: Second Son and Marvel's Wolverine stable enough to play. Before Claude was pulled into the picture to generate fixes, games like Demon's Souls couldn't even reach the character creation screen on PC.

As PS5 emulators make strides, Sony is also contending with worrying progress on the PS5 jailbreak front. Breaking free from the hardware ecosystem has been possible for a while now, but pulling it off has been somewhat prohibitive for average gamers. A new exploit called Relapse allows PS5 owners to gain kernel access to the system without the use of a PC, straight from the console's own interface. Hackers do have to use systems with older firmware, but the firmware version number is recent enough that most of the PS5's major releases this year could be pirated on the platform.

Relapse was authored by humans, but the exploit is inextricably linked to AI. Jailbroken devices make it possible for vibe coders to make and distribute emulators, recompilation projects, and other home-brew apps that would normally take a long time to develop. And users can get Super Mario ported to PS5 while optimizing those game files to be nearly 50% smaller than their official counterparts.

These are all unprecedented innovations, but they come with caveats. Many of the viral projects aren't necessarily playable public experiences, nor are they fully stable builds. Still, if this is what is possible in only a few weeks after a major AI breakthrough, one can only imagine where things will be a few months from now. DMCA takedowns can only go so far when seemingly no game is safe. Factor in that the law hasn't quite caught up with AI developments, and you've got to imagine this ordeal has gaming executives sweating.

Yes, you read that right… FromSoftware 's notoriously brutal combat in Bethesda's, uh, far more forgiving formula. A fan reveals the mod over on X , noting that it's "fully playable," with a clip of the crossover creation in action. "This isn't a passthrough or any fancy tricks," they write. "Someone straight up remade Elden Ring's player controller in Rust and can now be added to any game!" So, put simply, this is the product of players themselves.

There's the first, "Funny-Bones" over on GitHub , who conjured up the "Elden Ring player movement and combat," as he calls it, using Rust – a programming language, which can then be applied to virtually any other game. Then, there's the modder who did just that, leading to the impressive video of the Dovahkiin fighting Tarnished-style that's circulating social media now. It's impressive, and doubly so considering the whole generative AI trend.

Skyrim x Elden Ring 🚨 Elden Ring combat is now FULLY playable in Skyrim via a mod. This isnt a passthrough or any fancy tricks. Someone straight up remade Elden Ring's player controller in Rust and can now be added to any game! https://t.co/lxRH8kGVYR October 6, 2026

You know, the one that's seeing countless people try and generate games into other games? If you're lucky enough to have not witnessed it yet yourself, it basically involves folks taking popular titles and merging them with others. For example, just have a look at this post that supposedly shows "the entire" Minecraft game running in Elden Ring. Spoiler alert: it's AI slop, and not a playable mod at all, unfortunately.

The Skyrim mod should be, though, as its poster notes he'll be uploading it "soon" – and fans are, well, fans . One person puts it perfectly in the replies: "Holy peak." Others dub the project "insane," while more comment on how "cool" it is. As for when we'll all get to check it out for ourselves, there's no telling. Fingers crossed it's soon, because who doesn't love dying to a mere bandit a million times over?

(Image credit: FromSoftware) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter By building out studios and staying focused on genres, Tencent hopes to create the next Larian or FromSoftware , developers capable of releasing year-defining hits like Baldur's Gate 3 or Elden Ring respectively.

That's according to Yong-yi Zhu, Tencent Games VP and head of operations, strategy, and compliance, who spoke to The Game Business about the Chinese company's plans both globally and domestically.

Tencent, which holds substantial investments in numerous studios around the world, now including a new subsidiary of Assassin's Creed maker Ubisoft , sees those exact mega-RPGs as "North Stars" for game development, Zhu says.

Rather than looking at games through a regional lens, Zhu says, "For us, it’s more about chasing high-quality talent and people that are bringing unique visions, have a very specific vision. We love to work with developers that are trying to hone their craft. The studios we cite as our North Stars, like Larian, FromSoftware, they've been in a particular genre for a long time and iterating on that genre."

Mechanically and stylistically, Baldur's Gate 3 was much closer to Larian's Divinity series than the original Baldur's Gate RPGs from BioWare . The studio's fingerprints were all over the IP, even if it was D&D at its core – not that that's a bad thing. Elden Ring, meanwhile, was essentially Dark Souls 4, 5, and 6 in a trenchcoat – a sprawling game combining everything FromSoftware had learned and tested in the action RPGs that led up to that point.

We won't get "the next FromSoftware" or "another Remedy or Larian" at this rate, warns veteran dev Former Dragon Age lead says Larian is taking a "risk" by making Divinity right after Baldur's Gate 3 Baldur's Gate 4 should just be an "oversized expansion pack for Baldur's Gate 3," BioWare vet says Tencent’s bid to create the next FromSoftware and Larian - YouTube Watch On Zhu says Tencent wants to find developers who can do the same. It's important to note that the company also owns minority but significant shares of Larian as well as FromSoftware owner Kadokawa. Last year, Tencent increased its ownership in Kadokawa further, years after it and Sony increased their ownership of FromSoftware itself .

"For us, we try to do the same thing with our internal studios," Zhu continues. "We want to work with you if you believe one day you can be the category leader in this particular genre. That could be today, two games from now, or three games from now, as long as we see that progress. That is the long-term commitment."

Zhu uses these same franchises as examples of how studio given long-term support can produce generational hits. "You look at those two partnerships specifically, it wasn't an overnight success," he says. "It was multiple Divinities into Baldur's Gate. It was Demon's Souls into Dark Souls into Bloodborne and then finally into Elden Ring, which was so big. We do have a long-game approach. That's one thing that I think is very unique to Tencent and suits us well in working with a number of different developers for a long time to come."

After Baldur's Gate 3's explosive success, Larian has split with Wizards of the Coast and returned to Divinity. FromSoftware used some its Elden Ring bucks on stranger games like Elden Ring Nightreign and The Duskbloods , but also seems to have another single-player epic in the chamber.

A key distinction with Tencent, as Zhu notes, is that "a lot of our games are evergreen live service titles." He reckons this evergreen release schedule, as opposed to the huge dips and peaks that come when you release a new premium game every few years, provide some insulation against the waves of the industry at large.

Another way to minimize risk, he says, is to scale down development teams during "the riskier part of the project," which is generally early in concepting and pre-production. Increasingly, we see pushes for smaller game development teams , with many such teams finding outsized success every year.

Tencent hasn't been able to avoid the contraction in the games industry. Game dev layoffs look particularly devastating when you isolate them to the United States, but it's also tumultuous across the world, with Tencent reportedly backing out of multiple studio deals this year and closing TiMi Montreal, a studio helmed by Assassin's Creed: Black Flag director Ashraf Ismail, before it released a game .

items.title: New Elden Ring Mini Replicas Arrive: Malenia, Messmer & Wylder
items.summary: Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the l
items.content:
Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

Which replica will earn a place on your shelf?

items.title: I Tested Elden Ring On Switch 2 In A Cozy Cafe And It Ran Just Fine, Which Is Great News For A Remarkable Game
items.summary: You shouldn't play it in the rain/but you can play it on a train
items.content:
Elden Ring is an excellent, excellent video game. It’s got that smashy FromSoftware combat, a couple hundred boss fights that are all (mostly) unique and fun, character build customization for miles, a gorgeous and massive open world that’s a treat to explore, an intriguing story and hidden secrets, and a robust DLC that could be a game all its own. There’s a reason (well, many reasons!) why it’s almost universally critically acclaimed and still beloved by fans a few years after launch, too.

I love Elden Ring ! But when Ethan asked me to take on the review of the Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2, I wasn’t, like, stoked about it. I beat Elden Ring back when it first came out, easily dumping over 100 hours into the main game and probably another solid 40 or more into the DLC. And I played the Tarnished Edition at a preview event earlier this year for about 20 minutes, after which time I told everyone I spoke with about the experience that yup, that was Elden Ring all right! Elden Ring on a Switch 2! Game’s great, but I don’t necessarily need to play it again. What else is there to say?

It turns out, after playing for review, I do have one additional thing to say: Elden Ring is, apparently, pretty fun to play in public. Ideally at a cozy coffee shop with squoshy chairs where you can purchase hot London fogs to drink while you play.

Elden Ring was technically playable on the go before the Tarnished Edition , for folks with a Steam Deck. I have one of those, but the device, unlike the Switch 2, is not fun to take out in public. It’s heavy to hold, does not have a convenient kickstand, and you have to hold it in your hands to play if you don’t want to drag a controller around too. With the Switch 2, I could set the console on the table with the kickstand out, take the Joy-Cons off, lean back in my chair, and play Elden Ring while soothing cafe music played in the background. Every time I die (which is often), I get a nice sip of tea. I do not rage. I do not tense up. Helpfully, the cat (who is not here in the cafe with me) does not butt her head against the triggers and cause me to swing my sword randomly. Life is good.

In basically every other respect, I stick to my guns from the preview: this is Elden Ring ! It’s on the Switch 2 now! There were concerns after the first round of early previews that it ran poorly, but those were fixed by the time I previewed it earlier this year and remain fixed now. It runs fine. There are still occasional little framerate drops and yeah, it doesn’t look quite as nice as it will on your PS5 or Xbox Series, but who cares? It still plays great. The minor technical compromises didn’t interfere with combat in any way that was meaningful to me. It still looks good. It’s still lovely to stand on a cliff’s edge and look out in the direction of the Erdtree, the sun’s rays glistening through the clouds and a skyline of crumbling ruin all around.

I should mention that the Tarnished Edition does not have any meaningful new features. There are four new armor sets, a bit of customization for Torrent, and two new starting classes. Unfortunately, two of those new armor sets are starting sets for the two new classes, Heavy Knight and Idus Knight. I played as the Idus Knight and replaced my armor almost immediately with some tunic thing I got off a knight in the very first part of Limgrave, because it had better stats. I think I wore this same tunic when I played the game the first time. Shame, because the new starting armor genuinely looked great. I found the addition of these two new classes to be extremely whatever: you’re going to customize all your stats and replace all your gear almost immediately anyway. The Idus Knight was just a Samurai two levels lower, with different equipment. These additions did nothing for me, and certainly will do nothing for anyone after the first hour of game.

This release does include the superb Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, bundled right in from the start, though. That rules.

But who cares? It’s Elden Ring , on Switch 2! I can easily play it on a plane or on a train, in a box or with a fox, here or there, anywhere! I can take it to bars, to rooftop wine parties. I can play it outside on a patio with a cold one in a koozie next to me as the summer sun sets. I recognize that this is just effectively restating the main gimmick of the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2, but I admittedly haven’t taken my Switch 2 out much since it launched last year. Elden Ring , the best game of 2022 and arguably one of the best games of the decade, is a great excuse to do so. Give it a shot. Order yourself a latte or, a little later in the day, maybe a nice glass of pinot noir, bust out your Switch 2, and give it a shot.

This article was corrected post-publication: Limveld is Nightreign , Limgrave is Elden Ring . I can never keep them straight.

Who among us doesn't love to sever the Dreadnodus?

(Image credit: Hoyoverse) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter As the opening reveal of this year's Gamescom Opening Night Live, HoYoverse brought its first official look at Nodusfall—a change of pace for the gacha game behemoth that looks a little bit Elden Ring , a lot bit Monster Hunter, and a whole pile of proper nouns added for good measure.

While I like to think it takes more to catch my attention than forcefully mashing together two things I think are neat, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't tempted by the idea. If there's one thing Monster Hunter monsters have been missing, it's FromSoft-style primordial depression.

Watch On From the looks of things, there's more than enough metaphysical malaise to go around in Nodusfall. The laws of divinity have apparently frayed, plunging creation into a state of cosmic disarray. There are 10 suns now. Ideally, there's only supposed to be one of those. Not great!

Luckily for those of us who like to be given an excuse to try to fight a lizard 30 times our size, all that profound devastation seems to have produced a wide selection of giant, charismatic creatures to swordfight alongside your friends. In the reveal trailer embedded above, I saw giant bears, some sort of giant pack foxes, a horned, winged manticore, and a dragon or two (giant). I don't yet know how Nodusfall's progression works, but if I'm not allowed to harvest all their individual pieces and turn them into pants, I'm going to feel personally betrayed.

While the glimpses of combat shown in the footage looks like it hews pretty closely to the pace and rhythm of Monster Hunter, Nodusfall does seem to be dropping a few original elements into the mix. At one point, one of the player characters uses some sort of transformation ability to become a giant, armored knight in the middle of a hunt. And later, two players perform an elaborate, paired execution animation.

Nodusfall isn't Elden Ring, Monster Hunter or a typical HoYoverse game—it's something very different HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' All the key details on HoYo's co-op monster slayer Nodusfall What remains to be seen is what sort of monetization scheme Nodusfall will be wrapped in—something that HoYoverse's history doesn't exactly inspire confidence about. If I have to do gacha pulls for a gunlance, I'm going to have a hard time.

Nodusfall doesn't have much of an online presence yet, so it'll likely be a while before we can expect a release date.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stormveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one.
